justification: Thesis ratifies the restructured book: nine sections x four prayers = 36 total. Eight moments of the day plus the clockless Anytime pocket; the intro and blurb derive from this structure.

Mood, not moment. Practical Prayers is a clock book; solitude is an emotional state and states belong to Tantric Prayer's rasa ladder (Karuna/Shanta cover the inner weather). Its four entries move to stale.py.
Same class as alone: boredom and blankness are emotional states, not moments of the day. TP's rasa structure owns states. Its four entries move to stale.py.

Renamed from Positive in an earlier pass but still an emotion-section — positive/negative mood twins were always TP territory (Adbhuta/Vira), and the owner ruled them out of the clock book entirely. Its four entries move to stale.py.

The ninth section breaks the clock pattern on purpose: short portable mantras you can do all day — the one section not tied to a moment. Admits only pocket-length recitations; becomes the home for usable Swamiji hymns leaving TP's Sangha.

The canonical five-syllable mantra, owner-ordered into Anytime as the pocket prayer par excellence — recitable in two seconds, no clock, no verse needed. Sourced extract-and-place from anthology sources/mantras.json + namah-shivaya.json (copy into PP sources); NOT agent-written.
Its own text says it should be recited in EVERY ACTION — definitionally an anytime mantra, not a rasa verse. Leaves TP's Sangha (owner-ruled out of the rasa book) and lands in PP's clockless pocket.

The Secret Remedy: pacifies all sins, removes all sorrows — remedy logic is moment-independent, so it belongs in Anytime. Leaves TP's Sangha per owner ruling; sources (bahurupa-meaning.pdf) copy over with it.
Shortest sangha hymn (69 IAST chars) with viniyoga in the recitation PDF — pocketable at last, where the long dhyana mantras were not. Leaves TP's Sangha per owner ruling.
